title: Yaudheya Republic
capsule: The Yaudheyas were a kshatriya warrior republic (gaṇasaṅgha) occupying the eastern Punjab and Haryana region, attested from the Mauryan period and prominent through the Kushan and Gupta eras. Their coin series, stamped with the legend "Yaudheya gaṇasya jaya" (Victory to the Yaudheya republic), document a sustained civic identity across several centuries. They withstood incorporation by the Kushan Empire and continued issuing coinage into the late 4th century CE, after which Gupta expansion under Samudragupta (r. c. 335–375 CE) absorbed or subordinated the northern gana-states. Their political extinction left no textual chronicle; the record is essentially numismatic.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; boundaries are inferred from coin-find distributions in Haryana and the upper Gangetic plain, with no contemporary map or detailed textual demarcation surviving.
